newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil up sharply in Europe on Indonesian move.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil up sharply in Europe on Indonesian move.

text.p: News that Indonesia's joint marketing agency (KPB) had suspended October exports of crude palm oil triggered a $15 a tonne rise in crude palm oil prices on the European market in early Wednesday dealings.
But traders saw this as a knee-jerk reaction to confirmation of talk that had been in the market for two to three weeks.

"October has been moving into a premium for a while now because most people realised that sooner or later the Indonesians would have to do something about the oversold July, August and September positions," said a trader.
A KPB official told Reuters in Jakarta that the suspension would allow it to meet a backlog of previous commitments.
However, traders doubt there will be any long-term effect on the market.
"The KPB only accounts for 35 percent of Indonesia's exports with the private sector making up the other 65 percent, so any slack could be made up by them," said a Singapore-based trader.

Traders said exports from Indonesia were expected to be low during October due to the increase in export duty on crude palm oil during September to $36 a tonne, which they expect to carry forward into October.
"With almost 56,000 tonnes of crude palm oil sitting in the Rotterdam tanks and a lot more oil already at sea l can't see the European market getting very worried about this," one said.
Traders added that the only people who could be concerned are the shorts in the paper market.
"It could worry a few people in the paper market but the physical side should not have any problems," another said.
If the rise in prices was sustain the KBP could be tempted back into the market.

"There could come a point where prices in Malaysia will be at a level to make it worthwhile for the KPB to sell oil again before the end of October, so it's in the Malaysian traders' own interest not to push prices too high," said another trader.
